Rendered from the design at low: treatment-by-time growth with random subject intercept and slope. baseline is the week-0 sbvalue copied onto every row (alternate/derived response), ignored to avoid collinearity. Source Vonesh & Chinchilli (1997). Second reading #22: the pre-treatment baseline is a covariate, not an alternate response.

formula: vsae ~ age2 * sicdegp + I(age2^2) + (0 + age2 + I(age2^2) | childid)
notes: Help page describes a longitudinal autism study (Vineland socialization vsae by age) but gives no formula; the model is from West, Welch & Galecki (the kwelch source). sicdegp is labelled a plain factor (low/med/high), not an ordered factor, so no type declared. gender, race and bestest2 are unused but usable columns. Hand sample #12: the cited book's final chapter 6 model removes the random intercept and the quadratic-age-by-group fixed interaction.

Canonical Gelman & Hill (2007) varying-intercept radon model: floor indicator basement (within county) and county-level soil uranium, random county intercept. The response is already in log pCi/L (no raw radon column). county.name is the county label (alternate id), ignored. Published Stan/ARM example model.

Help page gives lmer(lnw ~ exper + (exper | id)) in a dontrun block. Singer & Willett (2003) ALDA wage-trajectory example; response is log wages. hgc.9 (centered hgc) and the ue.* columns are transforms of hgc and uerate (derived), ignored; ged, postexp, black, hispanic, hgc and uerate are unused but usable columns.

glmmTMB help example owls_nb1 (nbinom1, zero-inflation ~1; Zuur et al. 2009). BroodSize enters as offset(log(BroodSize)) but is a model column, listed under covariates (gopher rule). NegPerChick (=SiblingNegotiation/BroodSize) and logBroodSize (=log(BroodSize)) are derived, ignored; ArrivalTime is an unused usable column. The update owls_nb1_bs moves the offset to a log(BroodSize) covariate, not filed as a second model.

formula: count ~ spp * mined + (1 | site); zi = ~ spp * mined
notes: glmmTMB help example zipm3 (Poisson, zero-inflation ~spp*mined; Price et al. 2016, Dryad doi 10.5061/dryad.5m8f6). cover, sample, DOP, Wtemp and DOY are unused usable covariates left as columns. Hand sample #12: the documented zipm3 includes the spp:mined interaction in both the count and the zero-inflation components.

glmmTMB help example fm (nbinom2; Booth et al. 2003). Extended version of MASS::epil (different source; cross-source duplicate left to the merge). Base=log(base/4), Age=log(age), Visit=(period-2.5)/5 are the modelled transforms, so raw base/age/period plus lbase/lage (MASS transforms) and V4 (4th-visit indicator) are derived and ignored. subject coerced to factor in the example.

formula: abund ~ soil.dry + bare.sand + fallen.leaves + moss + herb.layer + reflection + (1|id) + (1|Species)
notes: Help page gives no model (CANOCO spider data in long form, via mvabund). RULE GAP: model rendered from the design at low; abund (count) response, environmental variables (log-transformed per CANOCO) as site-level covariates, id (site) and Species inferred as crossed random intercepts from the column names and the known 28-site 12-species spider data.

documented_prior: set_prior("normal(0,5)")
notes: brms help example fit2 (Poisson, varying patient intercepts; Breslow & Clayton 1993, Thall & Vail 1990). fit1 has no random effect, not filed. zAge/zBase are the standardized Age/Base the model uses, so Age and Base are ignored; obs is the row id; visit (1-4) is an unused usable time column.

documented_prior: set_prior("normal(0,5)")
notes: brms help example fit2 (cumulative ordinal, varying subject intercepts; Ezzet & Whitehead 1991). rating is a 1-4 ordinal rating (stored numeric). fit1 (sratio, no random effect) not filed. treat/period/carry are the two-period crossover contrasts.

documented_prior: set_prior("cauchy(0,2)", class = "sd")
notes: brms help example fit2 (Weibull frailty, varying patient intercepts; McGilchrist & Aisbett 1991). RULE GAP: censored survival response (time | cens(censored)), not a standard GLMM; filed for the patient grouping, response_type continuous (survival time), the censored indicator ignored. recur (1st/2nd recurrence) is an unused usable column.

formula: cum ~ ult*(1-exp(-(dev/theta)^omega)); ult ~ 1+(1|AY); omega ~ 1; theta ~ 1; Gaussian, nl=TRUE
documented_prior: c(prior(normal(5000, 1000), nlpar = "ult"), prior(normal(1, 2), nlpar = "omega"), prior(normal(45, 10), nlpar = "theta"))
notes: NONLINEAR: brms help example fit_loss (Gaussian nonlinear; Gesmann & Morris 2020, hierarchical compartmental reserving). Cumulative loss cum grows with development month dev. premium is an unused usable column. Confidence capped at medium by the nonlinear rule. Hand sample #11: theta and omega are estimated population-level nonlinear parameters with normal priors, not fixed constants; ult has an origin-year varying intercept.

Help page gives no model (A-not-A-with-sureness discrimination design; Christensen, Cleaver & Brockhoff 2011). Model recalled at medium from that paper and the ordinal package clmm worked example: ordered 6-level SURENESS ~ PROD with random respondent intercept (1|RESP). PRODID, DAY, SOUPTYPE, SOUPFREQ, COLD, EASY, GENDER, AGEGROUP and LOCATION are unused usable covariates. Domain psychology_neuroscience for the perceptual discrimination task (reporting only; Unilever consumer research, could read as industry).

Help page fits clm(rating ~ temp*contact) with no random effect. RULE GAP: that model has no grouping factor, so the registered model is the judge random-intercept version recalled from Tutz & Hennevogl (1996) and the ordinal clmm worked example. rating is the ordered 5-level grouping of the continuous column response (ignored). bottle (8 levels) is an unused usable column. Domain industry for the wine-production process factors (reporting only; could read as agriculture).

geepack help example fit (ordgee, exchangeable). The source fits a GEE; its cluster id is the grouping factor, given here as the lme4-equivalent random intercept (1|id). y is an ordered 3-level response; day is modelled as a factor. Ordinal Data from Koch.

formula: numobese ~ gender + cage + cage2 + gender:cage + gender:cage2 + (1|id)
notes: geepack help example gee2 (geeglm, binomial, independence). The source fits a GEE; cluster id given as (1|id) (Woolson & Clarke 1984; Fitzmaurice ALA). numobese (0/1) response; obese is its yes/no twin, ignored. Formula verbatim uses cage=age-12 and cage2=cage^2 (derived from age), so the age polynomial reduces to the column age. occasion (wave) and base_age are unused usable columns. gee1 (numobese~gender) not filed as a second model.

geepack help example fit.ex (geeglm, binomial, exchangeable). The source fits a GEE; cluster id given as (1|id) (Fitzmaurice & Laird 1993). resp is binary wheeze status; age is centred at 9 years. A subset of the external six-city study (kept, not a same-source derivation).

geepack help example gee.exc (geeglm, binomial, exchangeable). The source fits a GEE; cluster id given as (1|id); 111 patients from two clinics. outcome is binary respiratory status. center is a fixed covariate as modelled (not a random effect); sex and visit are unused usable columns. The aliased respiratoryWide is not a separately enumerated object.

geepack help example geese fits fit.88/fit.89 (GEE, AR1) with cluster id = tree (Diggle, Liang & Zeger 1994); the survey adds the chamber the trees sit in (four chambers, ozone assigned at chamber level, so chamber inference is weak; spot check #22). contr=1-(ozone==enriched) is derived from ozone; the example splits spruce into sitka88 (wave<=5) and sitka89 (wave>5), the survey uses the full table. Confidence medium for the lme4 translation of the subset GEE fits.

Help page gives no model (only coplot/qplot of Weight~Time faceted by Evit*Cu; Lauridsen et al. 1999). RULE GAP: model rendered at low from the 3x3 factorial weekly-growth design; Weight (continuous) on Time, Evit and Cu with pig random intercepts, pigs nested in litters ((1|Litter)+(1|Pig)). Feed (cumulated intake) and Start (week-1 weight) are unused usable columns. Second reading #22: Start (weight at the start) is a baseline covariate.

Help example m1 lmer(yield ~ -1 + trt + (1|rep/mp/sp)); mp=paste(row,spacing) and sp=paste(row,spacing,stock) are the main plots and subplots, so the grouping factors are rep and the composites row:spacing and row:spacing:stock (the merge builds them and the nesting). trt (factor) is the full treatment code 100*spacing+10*stock+gen; spacing and stock also enter the plot composites, gen and pos are unused columns. Cornelius and Archbold 1989 split-split-plot analysis.

Help page gives no model; alpha-design multi-environment trial (Buntaran 2020). Rendered with the three geographic zones fixed, genotype random (variety-trial BLUP reading) and the location, replicate-within-location and incomplete-block levels random; a genotype-by-location term (1|loc:gen) would be the more faithful MET model (second reading and adjudication #22).

Help example m0 lmer(yield ~ gen + (1|rep/block)); matches Burgueno et al. 2000 ASREML guide p.26. block (12 levels) nested in rep (3 levels, 4 blocks each); row and col are spatial coordinates used only by the asreml spatial models m1-m13, left as unused columns.

formula: yield ~ 1 + (1 | gen); residual covariance AR1(col) x AR1(row)
notes: Help example m2 asreml(yield ~ 1, random = ~ gen, resid = ~ ar1(xf):ar1(yf)) with xf/yf from col/row; matches Burgueno et al. 2000. 280 new genotypes are unreplicated with one check (G000) planted every 4th column, so gen is an almost-all-singleton grouping factor (only the check repeats) - an extreme imbalance case. row and col drive the spatial AR1 residual (not grouping); oddcol in m3 is built in the example, not a column. Hand sample #12: the selected documented m2 includes the spatial residual correlation the formula omitted.

Help example m0 asreml(yield ~ 1+env, random = ~ gen) - the base multi-environment model with genotype random and environment fixed; later models m1-m4 add a pedigree relationship matrix via vm(gen, ped.ainv), not a simple grouping. male and female are the diallel parents (components of the gen cross), left as unused columns. Butron et al. 2004.

Help example fits a fixed-effects lm(yield ~ 0 + gen + rep + cov) where cov is a derived average-neighbour covariate built in the example (not a column); Connolly et al. 1993. RULE GAP: no mixed model is documented; rendered from the four-rep single-drill RCB design with rep as a random block and variety (gen) fixed. matur (maturity group, constant within gen), row and col (spatial) left as unused columns.

Help example m2 lmer(yield ~ fert*soil*calcium + (1|rep) + (1|rep:fert) + (1|rep:soil) + (1|rep:fert:calcium)); the strip-split-plot of SAS/STAT guide example 23.5. The example drops the rep:soil:fert stratum for convergence (the afex block that adds it is inside if(0)).

Help example fits a fixed-effects anova lm(sqrt(white+.5) ~ rep + gen); Gomez and Gomez 1984 p.300, table 7.21. RULE GAP: no mixed model documented; rendered from the 14-variety, 3-rep RCB design with rep as a random block and gen fixed. white is percent white heads, modeled on the sqrt(white+.5) scale per Gomez; raw column white named as response.

Help example m1 aov(height ~ rep + manage + time + manage:time + Error(rep/manage/time)); Gomez and Gomez 1984 p.481, table 6.11. Translated to lmer: whole-plot management, sub-plot time, two subsamples per plot (the Within/residual stratum). sample (S1,S2) is the subsample index, left as an unused column.

Help example m0 aov(yield ~ nf*management*gen + Error(rep/nf/management)) with nf=factor(nitro); Gomez and Gomez 1984 p.143-153. Split-split-plot: nitrogen main plot, management sub-plot, variety sub-sub-plot; translated to lmer. nitro (5 doses) is used qualitatively as factor(nitro), so it is both a fixed factor and part of the whole-plot composite rep:nitro. col and row (field position) left as unused columns.

Help model m3l, the full-table lme (Schabenberger and Pierce 2002, p.518, proc mixed output 7.27): group-specific (age x species) quadratic trends in time with a random intercept and ti-slope per tree, plus a corExp(day|tree) residual correlation lme4 cannot express. ti=day/100 and ti2=ti^2 are built in the example from the day column. 40 trees (10 per species x age cell), repeated measures about every 5 days; the earlier models m1n/m1l/m2l fit the A2,S2 subgroup only and are not used (the survey uses the full table). Linear in parameters (polynomial in time), not nonlinear.

formula: adg ~ line + damage + line:damage + weanage + weight + (1|sire)
notes: Help example fits a fixed-effects lm(adg ~ 1 + line + sire + damage + line:damage + weanage + weight) with sire fixed; Harvey 1960 (an early least-squares-means paper). RULE GAP: rendered as the classic sire variance-component model with sire (9 sires, nested in the 3 dam lines) as a random grouping factor; the dmm package vignette (cited) gives a full mixed analysis. calf is the steer row id (ignored); weanage and weight are continuous covariates.

Jansen (1990) ordinal extravariation model; the help page fits no mixed model. Rows are cells of a contingency table (block x cross x category) with the number of plants in count, so the ordinal response is weighted by count (count in ignore as a weight) and each male-by-female cross defines a population, hence male*female fixed; the plot block:male:female is the random level. The measurer counts cells, not plants, as observations (adjudication #22).

Help example m1 clmm2(damage ~ rod + energy + gen + weight, weights=count, random=rod:energy, link=probit) and alternative m2 clmm(... + (1|rod:energy)); Keen and Engel 1997 (Statistica Neerlandica 51:129). Ordinal mixed model over an aggregated count table: damage D1<D2<D3<D4, count is the frequency weight (ignored). rod and energy are fixed and also form the random composite rod:energy; the weight column is the weight-class factor, not a model weight. Hand sample #61: the documented model weights each cell by count; counted once, a cell changes the likelihood, so no unweighted problem stands for it.

Help page gives no model (examples only desplot and group_by(gen) means); Kirk and Goulden 1925, a highly-replicated unrandomised variety trial with check plots every 5th row. RULE GAP: rendered from the variety-trial design with genotype (gen, varieties plus repeated checks) as a random grouping factor estimating variety means; the check varieties are far more replicated than the entries (imbalance). rep is labelled a replicate (not a block), row and col are spatial, left as unused columns.

Uniformity trial of barley; help examples fit an asreml model random=~x+y+ar1(x):ar1(y) with x=factor(col) and y=factor(row) (Piepho & Williams 2010). Random intercepts on row and col rendered in lme4; the separable AR1(col)xAR1(row) spatial term is not expressible and is dropped. Filed per the uniformity rule because the examples fit random terms on table columns (row, col). Hand sample #61: the source fits yield ~ 1, random = ~x + y + ar1(x):ar1(y), residual = ~units (asreml), x = factor(col), y = factor(row); dropping the separable spatial term changes the fitted model.

Multi-environment tomato trial (Ortiz et al. 2007); help fits PLS of the GxE matrix on environmental covariates (sibling ortiz.tomato.covs), no mixed model. Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the MET design; one yield per gen x env, some cells missing. weight is an alternate response, ignored.

Help fits a fixed betareg(y ~ gen + bunt + gen:bunt) on pct/100 and suggests bunt should be included as a random effect (Salmon 1938). Rendered with bunt random, the strong gen:bunt interaction as the random term bunt:gen and the layout repeat rep fixed (spot check #22). pct is a percentage, so continuous; infected and total counts are unavailable.
Help page fits lm(yield ~ rad + mint + I(mint^2)) and says a quadratic model makes no sense; rendered without the quadratic term, with locations nested in countries random (adjudication #22).

Split-plot repeated-measures asparagus (Snedecor & Cochran; O'Neill 2010). Help fits lmer(yield ~ trt + year + trt:year + (1|block) + (1|block:trt)) and an equivalent asreml split-plot; year is used as a factor. block:trt is the whole-plot composite built from its parts. An antedependence residual variant (m3) has the same random part, not a separate grouping.

Multi-environment potato trial (Tai 1971); yield is the mean of a 4-rep RCB at each environment, 48 genotype-environment cell means. variety is the genotype name (duplicate of gen); loc and year are the components of env; all ignored. Hand sample #11: the help gives a dotplot and a stability-analysis stub, not this crossed random-intercept model, which is proposed; Tai's stability analysis is not equivalent to it.

Dose-response of herbicide on larkspur in 3 reps (Turner et al. 1992). Help fits a pooled glm(prop ~ rate, weights=live, binomial) with no random term; rep (3 blocks) rendered as a random intercept. rate is a continuous dose. Response is dead out of live (binomial).

Multi-environment wheat trial (Vargas et al. 1998); help fits PLS of the GxE matrix on environmental covariates (sibling vargas.wheat2.covs). Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the 8-genotype by 21-environment design. RULE GAP: the stored yield is already environment- and genotype-centered (mean-zero GxE residuals, with negative values), so the main-effect variance components are near zero; the grouping dimensions are still real. Hand sample #12: the source fits PLS on the centred genotype-by-environment matrix, not crossed random intercepts.

Lattice-square variety trial of 49 soybeans in 4 reps (Weiss & Cox 1939). Help fits a fixed lm/asreml yield ~ rep + rep:col + rep:row + gen (matching Weiss table 7). Mixed rendering treats rep and the incomplete row/column blocks within rep as random, genotype fixed; rep:col and rep:row are composites built from their parts.

Classic Rothamsted split-plot (Yates 1935). Help fits lmer(yield ~ factor(nitro) * gen + (1|block/gen)) (m3); block/gen gives block and block:gen (whole plots). grain is yield in pounds (yield = 4*grain) and straw an alternate response, both ignored; row and col are plot coordinates left as unused columns. RULE GAP: nitro is modelled as factor(nitro) but stored as float, so the merge's column rule will count it continuous rather than a 4-level factor, and types cannot fix it on an R file (ordered only). Spot check #22: grain, straw and the plot coordinates row and col are ignored.

Help model m4 adds a linear col trend to m3 (better AIC), so col becomes a covariate. Same block and block:gen grouping; grain and straw ignored as in model 1. Same nitro-as-float RULE GAP noted for model 1.

Multi-environment powdery-mildew scores of 24 wheat genotypes (Lillemo et al. 2011); help computes nonparametric stability statistics and a GGE biplot, no mixed model. Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the MET design. RULE GAP: score is a mean across reps and each environment used one of four measurement scales (0-5, 1-9, 0-9, percent; the scale column), so the response is not on a common scale; the grouping dimensions are still real. Hand sample #61: the help uses transformations, GGE, median polish and ranks; the crossed random-intercept formula is inferred.

USDA state-level sorghum yields circa 1900-2011, one average yield per state per year. The help example fits a fixed piecewise regression to Illinois corn, not sorghum, with no grouping. state grouping with year as a time covariate rendered from the panel; acres harvested left as an unused column. RULE GAP: the response is a state-year average (aggregate statistic), not an observation-level measurement; filed for its longitudinal grouping. Hand sample #12: the sorghum random-intercept model is a reader proposal; aggregate yields may remain under the existing rule.

boot help (Davison & Hinkley): 14 location pairs, each a sign/no-sign site, measured at 3 periods, ~100 car speeds per set; design described, no model fitted. pair is the grouping; warning (sign presence) and period are within-pair covariates.

formula: cbind(r, n - r) ~ x + (1 | block) + (1 | var)
notes: boot help: randomized block design, 45 sugar-cane varieties x 4 blocks, diseased shoots r out of total shoots n (binomial); no model fitted. Rendered as random-effects GLMM per Census block-design rule; variety random (aim is to classify the 45 varieties by resistance), block random, x (stem pieces planted) a covariate.
boot help: 8 NBS experiments, each producing replicate estimates of g; one-way grouping by series (experiment), design described, no model stated.

boot help: tau-particle decay rates measured independently per decay mode (levels 1/rho/pi/e/mu), 6-19 measurements each; grouped by decay. Modes are distinct physical quantities, so the random-intercept-per-mode framing is inferred; design (repeated measurements per mode) is described.

lattice help: age-adjusted US mortality rates 2011-13 by HHS Region x Status (rural/urban) x Sex x Cause; help page gives only dotplot examples, no model. Region (10 levels) is the grouping; Status, Sex, Cause covariates; SE (standard error of the rate) ignored. Aggregate rates on a real grouping, low per Census rule.

lattice help: Immer Minnesota barley multi-environment trial, 10 varieties x 6 sites x 2 years, yield averaged across 3 randomized blocks; help page gives only a dotplot example. site is the grouping; variety and year covariates. Block-averaged aggregate response on a real grouping, low per Census rule. Hand sample #12: published_model no stands; the documented example is a dotplot.

formula: score ~ treatment + gender + phase + hour + (1 | id)
notes: Contrived repeated-measures data (O'Brien & Kaiser 1985, Psych. Bulletin 97), long form of OBrienKaiser; 16 subjects (id) measured across the within-subject factors phase (pre/post/fup) and hour (1-5), with treatment and gender between-subjects. The page describes the design (two between- and two within-subject factors) but gives no model formula; rendered as a subject random-intercept with the four factors as main effects. Full between x within factorial (treatment*gender*phase*hour) noted but not expanded into the interactions column. Hand sample #61: the additive subject-intercept formula is the reader's construction; the page states no model.

formula: piq ~ days + duration + sex + age + (1 | id)
notes: Longitudinal post-coma IQ recovery for 200 patients with traumatic brain injury (Wong, Monette & Weiner 2001, Brain Injury 15), 331 measurements (avg 1.7 per patient). Grouping factor id (subject); days = time post-coma (the longitudinal axis), duration = coma length, with sex and age. The page describes the longitudinal design but gives no explicit formula; rendered as a subject random-intercept. piq (performance IQ) filed as response; viq (verbal IQ, a parallel alternate response) in ignore.

formula: Claims ~ Pop_density + KI + Accidents + Population + (1 | SD)
notes: GAMLSS booklet data; de Jong & Heller (2007), Generalized Linear Models for Insurance Data, fit a claims GLM. The 176 local government areas are grouped into 13 statistical divisions (SD), the documented grouping; rendered as a random intercept on SD over the Claims count. LGA is a per-row area id; the L_ columns are logs of the covariates. Hand sample #61: de Jong and Heller fit Claims ~ L_Accidents + offset(L_Population) without random SD effects, population the exposure; the GAMLSS manual (p. 33) documents a model on logged population; neither supports the raw-scale random-SD formula.

Repeated height measurements of 197 girls with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, 1-21 per child (1988 obs); Durban (2016) fits P-spline growth curves. Grouping on case (child), with age and the 3-level treatment as covariates. The page says values were changed for confidentiality, not that they are simulated.

Hodges (1998, JRSS-B) hierarchical-model example: 341 federal-employee health-insurance plans within 45 states. The manuscript uses plan-level individual premium (prind) as response and individual enrollment (enind) as covariate, a random intercept on state. plan is a within-state code (row id); prfam and enfam are the family premium and enrollment alternates. State-level covariates (expe, region) are in hodges1, not this table.

Smoking-cessation meta-analysis (Silagy et al. 2003); random-effects logistic meta-analysis in Aitkin (1999) and Skrondal & Rabe-Hesketh (2004, GLLAMM). 27 studies (study = studyname x year), control/treatment (fac) fixed, quitters d out of n participants binomial. studyname and year are the components of the study id.

formula: rentsqm = beta0 + f1(area) + f2(yearc) + fgeo(district) + beta1*glocation + beta2*tlocation + epsilon; epsilon Gaussian
notes: Munich 1999 rent survey; rent is the alternate response. Hand sample #11: Fahrmeir, Kneib, Lang & Marx (2013), Example 9.2, Eq. 9.8: smooth effects of area and yearc, a district spatial effect by kriging at the district centroids (a structured covariance, so district stays the grouping factor), glocation and tlocation the good and top indicators derived from location. bath, kitchen and cheating are not in this model; Eq. 9.7 also omits the location indicators.

formula: time ~ age + xero + female + height + stunted + cosine + sine + (1 | id)
notes: Indonesian children respiratory-infection cohort (Sommer et al. 1983), 275 children up to 6 quarters; random-intercept logistic longitudinal model in Zeger & Karim (1991), Diggle et al. (2002) and Skrondal & Rabe-Hesketh (2004). The response column is named "time" (infection present, 0/1); grouping on id. resp is all ones; time.1, age1, season and time2 are time/id bookkeeping (season is represented by cosine and sine).

formula: bcnPower(exercise, lambda=0.25, gamma=0.1) ~ I(age - 8) * group + (I(age - 8) | subject)
notes: Fox & Weisberg, R Companion to Applied Regression 3e, chapter 7 (linear mixed models); help page describes the longitudinal design (repeated retrospective measures per girl, 138 patients and 98 controls) but states no model. Hand sample #12: the third edition's chap-7.R fits exercise on the bcnPower(lambda = 0.25, gamma = 0.1) scale, with subject intercepts and age slopes.

formula: decision ~ rater + nation + language + location + (1 | judge)
notes: Fox 2016 (Applied Regression Analysis and GLMs 3e) uses the refugee-appeal data to study whether judges differ; the documented fit is a fixed-effects logistic, rendered here as a random-intercept logistic on judge per the Census fixed-blocked rule. judge is in the grouping list (10 judges, 384 cases). success is a derived nation-level logit of success rate, ignored. nation kept as a covariate (could alternatively be a crossed grouping).

formula: headache ~ medication + treatment + sqrt(posttreat) + (treatment + sqrt(posttreat) | id)
notes: Fox & Weisberg, R Companion 3e GLMM chapter, uses the 133-patient migraine headache logs; binary headache (yes/no) over the repeated daily log entries by patient. dos (calendar time from study start) is redundant with time (days relative to treatment onset), ignored. Hand sample #12: the published final model (Fox, Appendix on mixed models) uses treatment = factor(ifelse(time > 0, "yes", "no")) and posttreat = pmax(time, 0), with random treatment and post-treatment trend effects; airq, hatype, age and sex are not in it.

Matched-pairs leukaemia survival trial, 21 pairs of two patients; documented survreg(Surv(time, cens) ~ factor(pair) + treat, exponential), rendered as random effects on the pair block (Census blocked-design rule). Censored response kept continuous with cens in ignore (Census brms-kidney rule).

Barley field trial, 6 locations (Loc block) x 5 varieties; yields stored wide for 1931 (Y1) and 1932 (Y2); documented aov(cbind(Y1,Y2) ~ Loc + Var) and aov((Y1+Y2)/2 ~ Var + Loc), Loc the block. RULE GAP: the documented response is both year columns or their mean, not one column; filed Y1 with Y2 in ignore. Hand sample #12: the help models both year responses or their mean with Loc fixed, not Y1 alone with a random Loc.

Speed-of-light measurements, five experiments (Expt) of 20 consecutive runs each; V&R MASS examine between-experiment variation of Speed by experiment, the help page states no model. Run is the within-experiment run index (ignore).

Snijders & Bosker running example, 2287 eighth-grade pupils in 132 classes; documented nlme::lme(lang ~ IQ*COMB + IQave + SES, random = ~ IQ | class). IQ centred within class; IQave is the class-mean of IQ (derived, not a table column); GS (class size) unused; random slope on IQ.

Classical NPK pea factorial on 6 blocks; documented aov(yield ~ block + N*P*K), block rendered as random (Census blocked-design rule). The fractional design confounds the N:P:K interaction with blocks; the reduced aov(yield ~ block + N + K) is a fixed-effects simplification (same model).

Matched case-control, 217 pairs (Kelsey & Hardy 1975); ID is the matched-pair grouping, each pair two rows. HSAUR3 conditional logistic clogit(status ~ driver + suburban + strata(ID)) rendered as random-intercept GLMM; model recalled from the book, help describes only the design.

Thall & Vail 1990; HSAUR3 Poisson GLMM glmer(seizure.rate ~ base + age + treatment + (1|subject), poisson). 59 patients, four two-week periods each. period is the within-subject time index, left as an unused usable column.

Four randomised Misoprostol-vs-placebo trials (Lanza et al. 1987-89); study (4 levels) the grouping subjects repeat within, treatment fixed, classification an ordered 5-level response. Help describes the design and shows per-study mosaic plots but fits no explicit model.

formula: status ~ centre + treatment + gender + age + month + (1 | subject)
notes: Multicentre longitudinal binary trial in long form (Davis 1991); HSAUR3 GLMM glmer(status ~ centre + treatment + gender + age + month + (1|subject), binomial). subject (111 patients) the random grouping; centre (2 levels) kept as a fixed covariate per HSAUR.

Longitudinal binary thought-disorder at 0,2,6,8,10 months for 44 women (Davis 2002); subject the random grouping, onset (early/late) the between-subject covariate. HSAUR3 Analysing Longitudinal Data (random-effects / GEE); model recalled from the book. Hand sample #61: the book's slides set this as a GEE exercise and state no random-intercept GLMM.
Faraway, Extending the Linear Model with R (ELM): one-way random effects on shift operator (a-d), 5 reps each. Hand sample #61: ELM fits bright ~ 1 + (1|operator) (the author's revisions page).

Faraway, Practical Regression and Anova using R, section 16.5: a balanced incomplete-block design, 6 diets over 10 litters of 3 (block); the documented fit is lm(gain ~ block + treat), blocks fixed. Hand sample #61: the claimed ELM mixed fit was not verified; the random-block formula is an adaptation.
Faraway ELM repeated measures with random slopes; 27 rats, 5 weekly weights, drinking-water additive. Model recalled from the book.
Faraway ELM longitudinal data; log income with person-specific intercept and year slope (the book centres year as cyear). Model recalled from the book.

Faraway ELM nested random effects; 7 subjects, both eyes at 4 lens powers, eye nested in subject. Hand sample #61: Faraway's rexamples (mixed/visionfreq.md) fits acuity ~ power + (1|subject) + (1|subject:eye).

Incomplete block design: plate (4 plates, 3 resistors each) is the block, shape (A-D) the treatment. No model stated; rendered as the random-effects version per Census blocking rule, fixed fit noise ~ shape + plate.

RCBD: 5 varieties across 5 plots (replicate = plot as block). failure is failures out of 100 seeds (binomial, 100 trials, but no trials column so filed count). No model stated; rendered random per Census blocking rule, fixed fit failure ~ variety + replicate.

Block = experimenter (blocking factor); Height, Frequency and resting heart rate fixed; Order is run order (ignored). No model stated; rendered random per Census blocking rule, fixed fit HR ~ Height*Frequency + RestHR.

Faraway ELM binomial overdispersion example (fixed fit glm cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ location + period). location = stream block (5), period = retrieval time; rendered with location random per Census blocking rule.

Repeated measurements of log-size on 79 Sitka spruce trees (54 ozone-chamber, 25 control), measured five times in 1988 (Diggle, Liang & Zeger, Analysis of Longitudinal Data; VR MASS 4th ed). Help page gives no model; rendered as a random-intercept growth curve with the ozone-by-time interaction, the grouping tree stated in the description. The size column is already on the log scale (holds log-size).

Repeated measurements of log-size on the same 79 Sitka spruce trees measured eight times in 1989 (Diggle, Liang & Zeger; VR MASS 4th ed). Companion to Sitka (1988 measurements), not a subset of it (different time points). Help page gives no model; rendered as a random-intercept growth curve with the ozone-by-time interaction, the grouping tree stated in the description. The size column holds log-size.

Help page fits the PQL GLMM glmmPQL(y ~ trt + I(week>2), random=~1|ID, family=binomial) (VR MASS 4th ed); documented model filed verbatim. ID is the child, 50 children checked at weeks 0-11. trt is a recoding of ap (active/placebo) and hilo (compliance), both ignored as alternate encodings. week enters via I(week>2), a transform of the week column.

formula: y ~ lbase * trt + lage + V4 + (1 | subject)
notes: Help page fits glmmPQL(y ~ lbase*trt + lage + V4, random=~1|subject, family=poisson) (Thall & Vail 1990; VR MASS 4th ed); documented model filed verbatim. subject is the epileptic, 59 patients over four two-week periods. lbase (centred log baseline count) and lage (centred log age) are the columns the model uses, so the raw base and age are ignored as their untransformed copies. V4 is the period-4 indicator. The within-subject index period is not in this model, left unused. The second glmmPQL(y ~ pred) is fit on an aggregated derived table epil3, not epil.

Inter-laboratory co-operative trial in analytical chemistry: seven specimens analysed by six laboratories in three batches each, every analysis duplicated (Analytical Methods Committee 1987; VR MASS 4th ed). Help page gives no model; rendered as a variance-components model with crossed laboratory and specimen effects and batch nested within laboratory-specimen (the duplicates are the within-cell replication). Bat is nested within Spc/Lab per the help, so the batch term is the composite Lab:Spc:Bat built from its parts. Hand sample #61: MASS (scripts/ch10.R) documents Conc ~ 1 with random ~1|Lab/Bat restricted to Spc == "S1"; that fit does not establish the all-specimen model.

Matched-pairs experiment: daily motorway accident counts on 92 days matched between 1961 and 1962, a speed limit in effect on some days (Svensson 1981; VR MASS 4th ed). Svensson's documented fit is a fixed-effects multiplicative Poisson model with day as a matched block; rendered here as the random-effects version with a random intercept per day per the blocked-design rule, year and limit the fixed covariates. Hand sample #61: the documented Poisson analysis (MASS exercise 7.7) treats the matched day as a fixed block; the random intercept is an adaptation.

Latin square (Davies 1954); help page gives no model. Faraway, Extending the Linear Models with R, crossed random-effects section fits lmer(wear ~ material + (1|run) + (1|position)): material the fixed treatment, run and position crossed random blocks.

Latin square design (Petersen 1994); help page gives no model. Rendered as the random-effects version per the Census blocking rule: inoculum (seed treatment) fixed, shade and irrigation the Latin-square row/column blocks random. Fixed model: lm(yield ~ inoculum + shade + irrigation). Hand sample #61: the source treats shade and irrigation as fixed blocks; the random-block model is an adaptation.

formula: disease ~ Sex + downs + Mray + MupRay + MlowRay + Fray + Cray + CnRay + (1 | ID)
notes: Matched case-control study (Le 1998); ID the matched pairs (a case and a control each, matched on age, race, county). Faraway ELM, Matched Case-Control Studies, fits conditional logistic clogit(disease ~ ... + strata(ID)); rendered here as a random-intercept logistic on ID for its grouping. age is a matching variable (constant within pair), left out of the model; CnRay is an ordered-factor covariate.

Latin square design (Lentner & Bishop 1986); help page gives no model. Rendered as the random-effects version per the Census blocking rule: supplier the fixed treatment, operator and day the Latin-square row/column blocks random. Fixed model: lm(y ~ supplier + operator + day).

Nested sampling design stated on the help page (Lentner & Bishop 1986): 3 growers selected at random, 4 boxes at random per grower, 3 clusters per box. Variance-components model with grower and box-within-grower (box 1-4 nested in grower, so the composite grower:box). cluster (1-3) is the within-box observation id, ignored.

Split-plot design (Cochran & Cox): recipe the whole-plot treatment, 15 batches of mix per recipe (the whole plots, so the composite recipe:batch), the 6 baking temperatures the sub-plot treatment randomised within batch. Faraway ELM split-plot example lmer(breakang ~ recipe*temp + (1|recipe:batch)); temp treated as a factor (6 levels). Hand sample #12: temp is numeric in the downloaded table, so the six-level temperature model needs an explicit factor conversion.

formula: I(CTSIB == 1) ~ Sex + Age + Height + Weight + Surface + Vision + (1 | Subject)
notes: Balance experiment (Steele 1998): 40 subjects, 12 measures each over Surface x Vision, twice. CTSIB is a four-point ordinal balance scale. Faraway ELM binary-response GLMM dichotomises it to stable = I(CTSIB==1) and fits a binomial glmer with a random Subject intercept; response column kept as the ordinal CTSIB. Surface and Vision vary within subject, Sex/Age/Height/Weight are subject-level.

Fully nested measurement-consistency design stated on the help page (Bliss 1967): 6 labs, 2 technicians per lab, 2 samples per technician (G/H, in fact identical), 2 replicate fat measurements each. Nested variance-components model; Technician (one/two) and Sample (G/H) nest within Lab, so the composites Lab:Technician and Lab:Technician:Sample.

formula: seizures ~ treat + expind + treat:expind + offset(log(timeadj)) + (1 | id)
notes: Longitudinal seizure-count clinical trial (Thall & Vail 1990): 59 patients, a baseline period and four treatment periods per patient (id the grouping). Faraway ELM Poisson GLMM example glmer(seizures ~ treat*expind + offset(log(timeadj)) + (1|id), poisson); timeadj (weeks of period) is the offset, age an available but unused covariate.

Chatfield, Problem Solving: A Statistician's Guide. 39 ankylosing-spondylitis patients, two sides (left/right) measured per person (78 rows). Flexion-after as response with flexion-before baseline; rotation angles rbef/raft are alternate responses ignored. Design described, no model stated; response chosen among the angle columns.

formula: narsp ~ ypc + perypc + regtest + rcdum + ajwtr + time + (1|msa)
notes: Frees, Longitudinal and Panel Data. 36 US MSAs over 9 years (324 panel rows), random intercept on msa; narsp is log average sale price, time is year 1-9.

Faraway, Extending the Linear Model with R (ELM): split-plot, irrigation the whole-plot factor on 8 fields, variety the split-plot factor. Design stated on the help page, lmer model recalled from the book.

Wedderburn (1974) quasi-binomial proportion example (also McCullagh & Nelder). 10 barley varieties at 9 sites, one obs per cell; blotch is a proportion with no trials column, filed continuous. Documented fit is fixed-effects on site and variety; rendered as random intercept on site (location block) per the Census blocking rule.

Randomized complete block design (Anderson & Bancroft): 8 oat varieties in 5 blocks (heterogeneous growing area). Documented analysis is fixed-effects (yield ~ block + variety); rendered as random intercept on block per the Census blocking rule.

Faraway ELM randomized block design (data from Box, Hunter & Hunter). blend (5 blends of variable corn-steep-liquor raw material) is the random block, treat (4 processes A-D) fixed. Hand sample #61: Faraway's rexamples (mixed/penicillin.md) fits yield ~ treat + (1|blend).

NIST Alaska-pipeline ultrasonic defect depths, field vs lab measurements taken in six batches (107 rows). Faraway fits a calibration regression Lab ~ Field ignoring batch; rendered with a random intercept on the named measurement Batch. RULE GAP: Batch is a data-collection batch, not a designed block.

Multicenter RCT (4 study sites) of rectal indomethacin vs placebo for post-ERCP pancreatitis (Elmunzer 2012 NEJM). Help gives no model; the trial compared treatment arms, rendered as a random intercept on site per the Census blocking rule. id is a row id whose first digit encodes the center.

formula: conc ~ biexponential two-compartment IV pharmacokinetic decay model (time); subject-specific coefficients
notes: NONLINEAR: IV indomethacin pharmacokinetics, 6 subjects, plasma concentration over time; nlme SSbiexp two-compartment model (Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Subject, time the nonlinear input.

Multicenter RCT (4 enrollment centers) of maternal periodontal treatment on pregnancy outcome (Michalowicz 2006 NEJM). Documented analysis: log-rank stratified by center and Cox proportional hazards; rendered as a linear mixed model with a center random intercept per the Census blocking rule. Gestational age censored at 37 wk, so Preg.ended...37.wk is the censoring indicator (ignored) and PID is a row id. Many baseline/visit periodontal covariates and alternate outcomes (Birthweight, Apgar) left as unused usable columns.

formula: weight ~ logistic growth curve (SSlogis) in Time; chick-specific parameters, Diet as a fixed effect
notes: NONLINEAR: chick body weight over time on four protein diets; nlme logistic growth SSlogis (help seealso), Pinheiro & Bates 2000 / Crowder & Hand 1990. Grouping Chick; Time the nonlinear input, Diet a between-chick covariate.

formula: density ~ logistic assay calibration curve (SSlogis) in log(conc); run-specific parameters
notes: NONLINEAR: ELISA assay of recombinant DNase, optical density vs known concentration across assay runs; nls SSlogis fitted per run, mixed over Run (Davidian & Giltinan 1995; Pinheiro & Bates 2000). conc is the nonlinear input.

formula: height ~ SSasymp(age, Asym, R0, lrc); fixed = Asym + R0 + lrc ~ 1, random = Asym ~ 1 | Seed
notes: NONLINEAR: loblolly pine height over age by seed source; nls SSasymp (Kung 1986; Pinheiro & Bates 2000). Grouping Seed, age the nonlinear input. Hand sample #61: the nlme help's model; refused at admission as nonlinear.

8x8 Latin square of honeybee repellent (lime-sulphur) potency; rowpos and colpos are the Latin-square row and column blocks, treatment (A-H) the fixed factor; rendered with row and column random intercepts per the Census blocking rule. RULE GAP: the census coordinate rule (besag.checks) sends a field layout's row/col to ignore, but here rowpos/colpos are the design's blocking factors rather than mere spatial coordinates, so they are filed as grouping factors. Hand sample #12: published_model no stands; the Latin-square row and column blocks and the continuous decrease kept, no trials.

Joyner-Boore ground-motion attenuation: peak acceleration at observation stations for 23 California earthquakes; observations repeat within event, analysed with random earthquake effects by Brillinger & Preisler (1984/85, cited). The published analysis is on log(accel) ~ log(dist); the raw columns are named. station (recording site) is a possible second crossed grouping but has many singleton levels and is left out; grouping inferred from the design, hence low.

Matched case-control of infertility after spontaneous and induced abortion; help fits conditional logistic clogit(case ~ spontaneous + induced + strata(stratum)), rendered as a random intercept on the matched set per the Census GEE/cluster rule. pooled.stratum is an alternate (pooled) matching id, ignored; age, parity and education are confounders used in an adjusted glm and left as unused usable covariates.

Student's sleep data: extra hours of sleep under two soporific drugs measured on the same 10 patients (ID); a paired design rendered as a random intercept on patient. The paired t-test in the help is the subject-random model; group is the drug.

formula: LogRT ~ PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + ReadingScore + OrthLength + I(OrthLength^2) + LogFrequency + LogFamilySize + (1|Word) + (1|Subject) + (0+LogFrequency|Subject) + (0+OrthLength|Subject) + (0+PC1|Subject)
notes: lmer from Perdijk, Schreuder, Verhoeven and Baayen (2006). I(OrthLength^2) is a quadratic on OrthLength (named once); random slopes on Subject add no grouping factor; PC4 and ProportionOfErrors are unused derived columns; Trial is unused but usable.

formula: LogRT ~ PC1 + PC2 + PrevError + Rank + ResidSemRating + ResidFamSize + LogWordFreq*LogAffixFreq*Sex + poly(LogCUP, 2, raw=TRUE) + LogUP + LogCUPtoEnd + (1|Subject) + (1|Word) + (1|Affix)
notes: lmer from Balling and Baayen (2008). poly(LogCUP,2) is a quadratic on LogCUP (named once). Hand sample #61: the three-way term LogWordFreq:LogAffixFreq:Sex added beside its pairs; the quadratic stays in the formula only.

formula: RealizationOfRecipient ~ AccessOfTheme + AccessOfRec + LengthOfRecipient + AnimacyOfRec + AnimacyOfTheme + PronomOfTheme + DefinOfTheme + LengthOfTheme + SemanticClass + Modality + (1|Verb)
notes: glmer binomial from Bresnan, Cueni, Nikitina and Baayen (2007). Speaker (spoken subset only, otherwise missing), DefinOfRec and PronomOfRec are not in the documented model.

Documented model is lm(DurationOfPrefix ~ Frequency + SpeechRate) (Pluymaekers, Ernestus and Baayen 2005), rendered as its random-effects version on the repeated grouping Speaker; Word is also a factor but not added as a grouping.

Documented model is lm(DurationOfPrefix ~ (YearOfBirth + SpeechRate) * Frequency) (Pluymaekers et al. 2005), rendered as its random-effects version on the repeated grouping Speaker; the help also fits fixed-effects models for PlosivePresent and DurationPrefixNasal, not filed as separate rows.

formula: RTlexdec ~ Voice + PC1 + MeanBigramFrequency + rcs(WrittenFrequency, 5) + rcs(WrittenSpokenFrequencyRatio, 3) + NVratio + WordCategory + AgeSubject + rcs(FamilySize, 3) + InflectionalEntropy + NumberComplexSynsets + rcs(WrittenFrequency, 5):AgeSubject + (1|Word)
notes: Documented model is a fixed-effects ols (rms) of RTlexdec, rendered as its random-effects version on Word (two subject-averaged rows per word, young and old). PC1 (first PC of the ten consistency columns) and NVratio (log NounFrequency/VerbFrequency) are constructed in the example and not table columns, so not filed; rcs splines named by their raw column; RTnaming and CorrectLexdec are alternate responses; aggregate response kept at low.

formula: RT ~ 1 + Correct + Trial + PrevType * meanWeight + Frequency + NativeLanguage * Length + (1|Subject) + (1|Word)
notes: lmer; worked example of the help (Baayen 2008, Analyzing Linguistic Data). Random-slope variants in the help keep the same grouping factors; meanRT is the by-item mean response; other by-item aggregates (SubjFreq, meanSize) and unused lexical columns remain usable. Hand sample #11: RT is already a log reaction time; it is not logged again.
lmer from De Vaan, Schreuder and Baayen (2007). Trial, Rating, Frequency, BaseFrequency, LengthInLetters, FamilySize and NumberOfSynsets are unused but usable.

lmer from De Vaan et al. (2007). PC1 (first PC of the four lagged RTs RT4WordsBack..RT1WordBack) is constructed in the example and not a table column, so neither PC1 nor the PC1:Condition interaction is filed; lagged and leading RT columns remain usable.
glmer binomial (O'Shannessy 2006). Sentence is a per-utterance identifier, ignored; OvertnessOfObject and AnimacyOfObject are unused but usable.

glmer Poisson from Keune, Ernestus, Van Hout and Baayen (2005). The random-slope variant (Country|Word) keeps the same grouping; Corpus is the newspaper whose Country and Register the model uses as fixed effects, not added as a grouping.

formula: Resp ~ nonlinear logistic threshold 0.5 + 0.5/(1 + exp(-(Loud-L75)/exp(lsc))) on trials-expanded binary responses from Correct of Trials; fixed L75 ~ Age, lsc ~ 1; random L75 and lsc by ID:Age; fit separately by Noise
notes: NONLINEAR: logistic threshold curve for probability correct in stimulus loudness Loud, subject-specific threshold L75 and slope lsc. Help page fits nlme(Resp ~ fp2(Loud,L75,lsc), fixed=L75~Age, random=L75+lsc~1|UID) on the trials-expanded binary data OMEf, in a dontrun block (fails on most platforms), per Noise subset; VR MASS 4th ed. UID is subject ID crossed with age, filed as the composite ID:Age. Native binomial response is Correct of Trials. The OME prevalence column enters only the second-stage lm(L75 ~ Noise/(Age + OME)), left unused. Hand sample #12: UID combines ID and Age; OME enters a separate regression on the estimated thresholds, not this nonlinear mixed model.

Nepali child health study (West et al. 1997, vitamin A and growth). Children (6-digit id) measured repeatedly over age (1000 rows); weight as response, height an alternate response ignored; died/alive are mother-fertility counts ignored. Design documented, model inferred. Second reading #23: model inferred, the simpler reading stands (age;sex).

Randomized complete block design (Mead et al. 1993): 12 pens, 4 blocks of 3 pens by location, 3 feed treatments (O/E/F). Mixed model lmer(eggs ~ treat + (1|block)): block random, treat fixed. eggs is a per-pen production total modelled on the continuous scale (Gaussian LMM). Second reading #23: response_type is what the column holds (egg totals), not the Gaussian fit.

lmer; Rating is a subjective size estimate on a seven-point scale modelled as Gaussian; MeanFamiliarity is a by-item mean familiarity used as a covariate. Second reading #23: response_type is what the column holds (a seven-point scale), not the Gaussian fit.

No model is fitted in the help (only a xylowess conditioning plot of Rating ~ Frequency | Subject); the crossed Subject/Word design with a seven-point weight Rating is rendered as a random-intercepts model at medium. Class (word attribute), Sex (subject attribute) and Trial (a trial index; the help field description is mislabeled) remain usable. Second reading #23: response_type is what the column holds (a seven-point scale), not the Gaussian fit.

Soil physical and chemical composition in a randomized block design: 4 blocks, 3 contours x 4 depths (Horton et al. 1968; Friendly 2006 JSS 17(6); Khattree & Naik 2000). Page states a two-way randomized block design and lists 9 response variables for MANOVA / canonical discriminant analysis, in page order pH, N, Dens, P, Ca, Mg, K, Na, Conduc. Rule (a) multivariate split: one row per response, model_index 1/2/3 = pH/N/Dens; the three-row cap leaves out P, Ca, Mg, K, Na, Conduc, filed in this row ignore with the derived group encodings Group and Gp. Census blocked-design rule: the fixed RBD is rendered as a Block random intercept at low confidence. Depth is quantitative on the page but not stored as an R ordered factor, so no types declared. Hand sample #61: the source fits Block as fixed in its MANOVA (Friendly 2006, JSS 17(6)), so the random-Block formula is a proposal.

Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Soils: response N (total nitrogen in percent). Same randomized block design as model_index 1 (see the pH row); the other eight chemical responses and the derived encodings Group, Gp in ignore. Hand sample #61: the source fits Block as fixed in its MANOVA (Friendly 2006, JSS 17(6)), so the random-Block formula is a proposal.

Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Soils: response Dens (bulk density in gm/cm^3). Same randomized block design as model_index 1 (see the pH row); the other eight chemical responses and the derived encodings Group, Gp in ignore. Hand sample #61: as Soils #2, the source fits Block as fixed in its MANOVA, so the random-Block formula is a proposal.

Chemical composition of ancient pottery from 4 British sites (Hand et al. 1994, A Handbook of Small Data Sets; a SAS manual MANOVA example; suggested by Friendly). Multiple samples repeat within Site. Page lists 5 chemical response variables in page order Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na with no covariates. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = Al/Fe/Mg; the three-row cap leaves out Ca, Na, filed in this row ignore. Census fixed-design-to-random rule: the one-way Site layout is rendered as a Site random intercept at low confidence. Hand sample #61: as Pottery #2, the source fits Site as fixed in its MANOVA.

Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Pottery: response Fe (iron). One-way Site random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al); the other chemical responses in ignore. Hand sample #61: the source fits Site as fixed, Fe ~ Site as the iron part of its MANOVA.

Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Pottery: response Mg (magnesium). One-way Site random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al); the other chemical responses in ignore. Hand sample #61: as Pottery #2, the source fits Site as fixed in its MANOVA.

Romano-British pottery, chemical composition by atomic absorption spectrophotometry for nine oxides, specimens grouped by kiln / find-site (Tubb, Parker & Nickless 1980, Archaeometry 22; HSAUR3 MANOVA / cluster example). Page lists nine oxide responses in page order Al2O3, Fe2O3, MgO, CaO, Na2O, K2O, TiO2, MnO, BaO and kiln as the site factor. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = Al2O3/Fe2O3/MgO; the three-row cap leaves out CaO, Na2O, K2O, TiO2, MnO, BaO, filed in this row ignore. One-way kiln layout rendered as a kiln random intercept at low confidence; moved from the exclusions under rule (a). Hand sample #61: as pottery #3, HSAUR3 clusters the oxide measurements and fits no random-kiln regression.

Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 pottery: response Fe2O3 (iron trioxide). kiln random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al2O3); the other oxide responses in ignore. Hand sample #61: as pottery #3, HSAUR3 clusters the oxide measurements and fits no random-kiln regression.

Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 pottery: response MgO (magnesium oxide). kiln random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al2O3); the other oxide responses in ignore. Hand sample #61: HSAUR3 clusters the oxide measurements hierarchically and compares the clusters with the kilns; it fits no MgO random-kiln regression.

Egyptian skull measurements from five epochs, 30 skulls each (Hand et al. 1994, A Handbook of Small Datasets; HSAUR3 one-way MANOVA example). The question is whether measurements change over time/epoch. Page lists four measurement responses in page order mb, bh, bl, nh with epoch as the time factor. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = mb/bh/bl; the three-row cap leaves out nh, filed in this row ignore. epoch treated as the grouping factor and the one-way layout rendered as an epoch random intercept at low confidence; moved from the exclusions under rule (a).
Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 skulls: response bh (basibregmatic height). epoch random intercept as in model_index 1 (mb); the other measurement responses in ignore.
Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 skulls: response bl (basialveolar length). epoch random intercept as in model_index 1 (mb); the other measurement responses in ignore.

RESPONSE INFERRED: nearly all 2017 Minneapolis Police Department stops (carData; public MPD open data). Page documents the records but names no model or response. Chose personSearch (whether the stopped person was searched, binary no/yes) as the outcome the data were collected to study (racial disparity in stops and searches), with neighborhood (84 levels) as the grouping factor and problem (stop type), race and gender as predictors. idNum row id, date, lat and long coordinates, policePrecinct (an alternate geographic grouping), preRace (the pre-stop race assessment), vehicleSearch and citationIssued (alternate responses) and MDC (collection method) in ignore.

formula: result ~ gender + pan_day + age + demo_group + patient_class + (1 | clinic_name)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: deidentified SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing at CHOP in 2020 (Obstfeld; medicaldata). Page documents the data but names no model or response. Chose result (test result positive/negative/invalid, three levels so filed categorical) as the outcome the data were collected to study, with clinic_name (88 clinics/wards) as the grouping factor and gender, pan_day (day of pandemic), age, demo_group and patient_class as predictors. subject_id and the fake first and last names (identifiers), test_id, ct_result (cycle-threshold, an alternate lab response), drive_thru_ind, orderset, payor_group and the two turnaround times col_rec_tat and rec_ver_tat in ignore.

RESPONSE INFERRED: performance of 595 players at the 2010 World Cup (faraway package; the page marks the source as lost). Page lists the variables but names no model or response. Chose Passes (count of passes made) as a player performance outcome, modeled on Position and Time (minutes played, an exposure) with Team (country) as the grouping factor. The other performance counts Shots, Tackles and Saves in ignore as alternate responses. Low: grouping and response inferred from the column names.

RESPONSE INFERRED: de Piles subjective 0-20 assessments of 54 classical painters on four characteristics, grouped by School (MASS / Venables & Ripley 2002; Weekes 1986; Davenport & Studdert-Kennedy 1972; Jolliffe 1986), a classic PCA example. Page documents no model or response. Chose Composition (the first characteristic) as the response on a School random intercept (8 schools A-H, painters repeat within school); the other three scores Drawing, Colour, Expression in ignore as alternate responses; no covariates. Scores are 0-20 integer ratings, filed continuous.

formula: hownbly ~ longlive + wherebfr + age + sex + (1 | district)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: questionnaire study of neighborly help in Exeter (Webley & Lea 1993, Human Relations 46; faraway package). Page documents the variables but names no model or response. Chose hownbly (the respondent rating of how neighborly their area is, 5-level ordinal from Vunfriendly to VFriendly) as the outcome the study measured, with district (4 described districts) as the grouping factor and longlive (time at address), wherebfr (previous location), age and sex as predictors. knowname and callname (how many neighbours known / addressed by first name) in ignore as alternate outcomes. The factor levels are naturally ordered but the page labels them factor, not ordered factor, so no types declared.

Faraway ELM nested random effects. 3 lawnmowers randomly selected per manufacturer (machine m1-m6, nested in manufact A/B), each tested twice at high and low speed. Model recalled from the book. Spot check #23 (Alex): each machine is tested twice at each speed, so machine:speed is the replicated within-machine stratum, a second grouping factor.

Junior School Project (Goldstein 1995, Multilevel Statistical Models, cited on the page).
